items.claim: The row dismisses an internal seam at 28:7 on the ground that no speaker, addressee or formula marks the turn, but 28:7 opens verse-initially with a contrastive particle plus a hear-this-word imperative and a second-person addressee, and no Hebrew is quoted from 28:7 or 28:8 at all.
items.evidence: 28:7 opens אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.28.7, byte) and carries the 2ms בְּאָזְנֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Jer.28.7, byte): a contrastive particle, a hear-the-word imperative with a demonstrative object, and an explicit addressee marking, standing verse-initially at exactly the internal turn the row rejects. That imperative shape is one of the internal onset classes the frame policy in force treats as a cut candidate, so the blanket ground that no formula marks the turn is contested by the bytes rather than merely under-argued. The row names the site's contrastive hinge in prose but supplies no form and no verse for it, and of the five verses in the span it quotes only 28:5, 28:6 and 28:9 - the two verses carrying the rival signal are the two left unquoted. The same imperative recurs eight verses later, שְׁמַֽע נָ֣א חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.15, byte), where a fresh Jeremiah-to-Hananiah address is treated as a seam in this same corpus; one device is being read two ways inside one scene. What does verify: the onset formula at 28:5 וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֖ה הַנָּבִ֑יא (oshb:Jer.28.5, byte), the ironic assent at 28:6 and the prophet-test at 28:9 are byte-exact, the close at 28:10 is byte-warranted by the return of Hananiah as actor, and the disclosure statement is accurate on all three single-witness layers - the parashah inventory, the paseq inventory and the ketiv/qere inventory are each empty at MT 28:4 through MT 28:9.

items.claim: The row labels Hananiah's formula at 28:11 the full divine formula carried again, but the bytes give the bare two-word shape there; the title stack he used at 28:2 is a different formula object, and the row's own splice in the same sentence contains no tsevaot.
items.evidence: 28:11 reads כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.28.11, byte). 28:2 reads כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.28.2, byte). The bare shape and the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack are separate book-wide count objects, so calling the 28:11 occurrence the full formula carried again imports the 28:2 form onto a verse that does not carry it; both witnesses agree, WEB rendering 28:11 as “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.28.11) against “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says,” (web:Jer.28.2). The row's own signal key names the bare shape, so key and prose disagree about the same site. Gloss extent also parts from splice extent at both ends of the same sentence: the Hebrew spliced runs from the formula through the king's name, while the English given drops the formula's own rendering at the front and adds “from off the neck of all the nations within two full years.” (web:Jer.28.11) at the back. What does verify, and is the row's real contribution: the mouth is Hananiah's, byte-anchored at the verse-initial וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲנַנְיָה֩ (oshb:Jer.28.11, byte); the counter-act at 28:10 is byte-exact; the vav-less defective name form נְבֻֽכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.28.11, byte) is byte-true, one of the two book-wide sites of that spelling (sweep: 2 verses, the vav-less defective name form); and the petuchah and the single paseq seg recorded at MT 28:11 both match the inventories under the types claimed.

items.claim: The boundary and its primary evidence stand, but the supporting notes call the second word-event site a closing device when its bytes make it a verse-initial onset opening three fresh verses, rank the pair above rivals never swept, and go silent on a paseq seg inside the span that the neighbouring unit discloses.
items.evidence: 29:30 reads וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.29.30, byte) - verse-initial, and followed by a fresh oracle in 29:31-32 - so it opens a word event and closes nothing; the same device is correctly read as an opener at 28:12 two sentences earlier in the same field. The pair-count itself is exact: this formula shape stands at exactly two sites across chs 27-29 (sweep: 2 verses, 28:12 and 29:30). The ranking of that pair as the strongest tier-1 signal available for any boundary across the three chapters is asserted without sweeping the rivals the bytes place beside it: 27:1 opens בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte) and 28:1 opens וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte), both verse-initial regnal-accession onsets with dated frames, both classified onset shapes in the same tier-1 system. Third, the single paseq seg recorded at MT 28:14 sits inside this row's own span and is undisclosed, while the unit covering 28:10-28:11 discloses exactly that object one verse earlier - an asymmetry inside one cluster. Fourth, the said-to-Hananiah recurrence between 28:5 and 28:15 is asserted untiered: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֖ה הַנָּבִ֑יא (oshb:Jer.28.5, byte) against וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֧ה הַנָּבִ֛יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא (oshb:Jer.28.15, byte) are identical at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers but differ in the pointed bytes at every word. What verifies: the word-event onset at 28:12 is byte-exact and an inventory member; 28:14 carries the full title stack; and the vav-less defective name form recurs at 28:14 exactly as claimed, the second of the book's two sites.

items.claim: The row discloses a setumah closing MT 28:16, but the single-witness parashah inventory records no mark of either type at that verse; the whole of MT ch 28 carries exactly two marks, both petuchah, at 28:11 and 28:17.
items.evidence: The WLC parashah layer keys each seg to the verse it closes. For MT ch 28 it holds exactly two entries - PE at 28:11 and PE at 28:17 (sweep: 2 marked verses in the chapter) - and nothing at all between them, so the claimed mark at MT 28:16 fails both arms at once: no mark stands at that verse under either witness reading, and the type asserted is not a type this chapter carries anywhere. The disclosure is framed as texture, which does not lower the bar: a single-witness mark citation either matches the inventory at the cited MT key or it does not. The unit covering 28:17 states in this same corpus that the inventory carries nothing at MT 28:16, so two statements about one verse contradict each other and only the negative one is inventory-true. Second defect: the row's actual seam warrant is the recurrence of the said-to-Hananiah formula from 28:5, given with no tier - וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֖ה הַנָּבִ֑יא (oshb:Jer.28.5, byte) against וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֧ה הַנָּבִ֛יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא (oshb:Jer.28.15, byte) are identical at accent_stripped and at skeleton tier, not at byte tier, and a recurrence carrying a boundary must name the tier at which it recurs. Third, the koh-amar at 28:16 is quoted byte-true but its mouth is never named at the formula itself, in the one chapter where the identical formula stands in a false prophet's mouth five verses earlier. What verifies: the 28:15 and 28:16 splices are byte-exact, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span, and the front-seam and interior absence statements are inventory-true.

items.claim: The one-verse unit at 28:17 verifies across the four arms checked - the mode shift, the date classification, the closing petuchah, and the stated absence of any mark at its front seam.
items.evidence: 28:17 reads וַיָּ֛מָת חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֑יא בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי (oshb:Jer.28.17, byte): a wayyiqtol third-person report with a same-year, seventh-month notice and no speech at all, which the date inventory classes as a narrative date rather than a header frame - matching the row's signal key rather than over-claiming a date-formula onset. The parashah inventory carries PE at MT 28:17 and nothing at MT 28:16, exactly the two statements the row makes, with the type named and single-witness weight disclosed; because the layer keys a seg to the verse it closes, that mark bears on the row's back seam only, which is what the row says it does. 28:17 closes the chapter in both witnesses (sweep: 17 verses in MT ch 28 and 17 in WEB ch 28), so the bounded-on-both-sides argument holds. No paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note stands in the verse. Residual, not a defect: the year word binds across the row's own front seam - the sentence at 28:16 runs הַשָּׁנָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה מֵ֔ת (oshb:Jer.28.16, byte) and the notice answers it with the same lexeme in וַיָּ֛מָת חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֑יא בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי (oshb:Jer.28.17, byte) - a byte-true catchword straddling the seam that argues mildly for fusion and is left undisclosed.

items.claim: The four factual arms of the three-verse superscription unit verify - the letter header, the absence of any speech formula across 29:1-29:3, both parashah marks under their claimed types, and the per-site name spellings including the later contrasting form.
items.evidence: 29:1 opens וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר (oshb:Jer.29.1, byte), naming the document itself, and the row's courier splice at 29:3 is byte-exact. No koh-amar and no imperative stands anywhere in 29:1-29:3 (sweep: 0 verses of either shape across the span), so the stated absence holds on a direct read of all three verses and the divine-voice address does begin at 29:4. The parashah inventory gives PE at MT 28:17 and SAMEKH at MT 29:3 under exactly the types claimed and in the closing-mark sense the row uses; no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span. The name claim survives per-site checking: 29:1 carries נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר (oshb:Jer.29.1, byte) and 29:3 carries the same nun-family vav-bearing form, and the claim that another spelling appears later in the chapter is byte-true - 29:21 carries the resh-family form instead. Residuals, not defects: the spelling asserted at 29:1 is not quoted at that site, the row's 29:1 splice stopping before the name, which leaves a per-site claim resting on assertion in the chapter run where that name's four attested spellings converge (sweep: 6 verses carry the nun-family form, all of them in chs 27-29); the modifier plene is elsewhere reserved for a different byform belonging to the other family, so the label crosses family lines; and 29:2 - a third of the span - is neither quoted nor characterised although it carries יְכָנְיָֽה הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ (oshb:Jer.29.2, byte), one of a single king's three name forms, and states a deportation date rather than the sender, recipients and couriers the row's summary enumerates.

items.claim: The row rejects the internal seam at 29:10 on speaker-and-addressee grounds alone, leaving undisclosed a three-signal convergence at the 29:9/29:10 juncture - a verse-final closure formula, a fresh speech-formula onset, and the mark the row does cite but without its direction.
items.evidence: 29:9 closes נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.9, byte) and 29:10 opens כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.29.10, byte). A postpositive closure formula standing verse-finally immediately before a fresh speech-formula onset is precisely the configuration in which that closure counts as unit-closing under the frame policy the row is working in, and the single-witness layer independently closes a seg at MT 29:9 - the row cites that mark but describes it only as falling inside the span, never that under the closing-mark reading it uses elsewhere it sits at the seam it is rejecting. The stated ground answers only frame-owner and addressee, and on those two points the row is right: the addressee is 2mp to the exiles at 29:4, 29:8 and 29:10 alike, and the speaker never changes. The row also leaves its own far seam under-argued in its own favour: 29:14 carries that same closure formula twice, נְאֻם יְהוָה֒ and נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.29.14, byte for each; the two occurrences are accent-distinct and identical only at accent_stripped tier), closure corroboration for the boundary actually drawn. Residual: 29:4 and 29:8 both carry the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack while 29:10 carries the bare shape, and the three are cited under one undifferentiated label. What verifies: the full title stack at 29:4 is byte-exact and correctly named; there are exactly three speech-formula sites in the span (sweep: 3 verses, 29:4, 29:8, 29:10); SAMEKH at MT 29:3, PE at MT 29:7 and SAMEKH at MT 29:9 all match under their claimed types; no paseq seg falls in the span; and the ketiv/qere at MT 29:14 is inventory-true with both forms - שביתכם שְׁבוּתְכֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.29.14, byte) - standing in the source bytes as quoted.

items.claim: At the one juncture the row declares undecided, it discloses the mark at 29:15 without its direction; under the closing-mark reading the row itself applies at 29:20, the marks at MT 29:15 and MT 29:20 segment 29:16-29:20 and place 29:15 with what precedes - and a second formula object and a rival onset inside the span go unquoted.
items.evidence: The single-witness layer keys a seg to the verse it closes, and in ch 29 records SAMEKH at MT 29:3, PE at 29:7, SAMEKH at 29:9, 29:15, 29:20, 29:23, PE at 29:29 and SAMEKH at 29:32 (sweep: 8 marked verses in the chapter). The row reads that layer as closing when it says a setumah closes the span at 29:20, and the neighbouring unit reads it the same way at 29:3; at 29:15 alone the row says only that a setumah falls in this opening verse. Under its own reading the 29:15 mark divides 29:15 from 29:16 and joins 29:15 to the preceding address - which is corroboration, weak and single-witness but real, for the very alternative the row says no evidence settles. The layer is never a driver and its absence is never counterevidence; the defect is the asymmetric disclosure at the crux, not the weight. Second, a distinct formula object stands unquoted inside the span: 29:16 opens כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.29.16, byte), the bare shape the row does quote, while 29:17 opens כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.29.17, byte) with tsevaot - a different object, undisclosed. Third, the span's own last verse opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.29.20, byte), a hear-the-word imperative with a vocative, standing immediately after 29:19, which carries the closure formula twice - נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה and verse-finally נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.19, byte for each; accent-distinct, identical only at accent_stripped tier) - so the bytes put a live rival seam at 29:19/29:20 that the row does not weigh while it does weigh 29:20/29:21. Fourth, the two paseq segs recorded inside the span at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 are undisclosed while the ketiv/qere at MT 29:18 is disclosed. What verifies: the 29:15, 29:16, 29:18 and 29:20 splices are byte-exact, both marks match under their claimed types, the ketiv/qere at MT 29:18 is inventory-true with both forms standing in the source bytes, and 29:21 does open a fresh speech formula naming two men as stated.
